memory_update.text: VRT remains the highest-purity public candidate for AI data-center power and thermal infrastructure; monitor backlog conversion and liquid-cooling capacity rather than treating backlog as guaranteed revenue.
ETN should be tracked as a grid-to-chip electrical equipment platform after Boyd Thermal; diligence should split core electrical backlog from acquired liquid-cooling exposure.

FIX maps to construction and MEP execution capacity; the key research question is whether technology-sector backlog is concentrated in AI/hyperscale data centers and whether labor/supply-chain constraints support durable pricing.

Future passes should separately test gas turbines, backup generation, nuclear/uranium, regulated utilities, data-center REITs, transformer specialists, EPC/grid-service firms and permitting/water-exposure names.

node: Data-center power, cooling, grid connection, and site infrastructure
summary: Layer 1B universe expansion for the AI data-center physical-infrastructure chokepoint. The strongest US-listed exposures in this pass cluster around: integrated power/thermal systems, electrical distribution and switchgear, liquid-cooling and rack-level power components, grid and utility electrical hardware, and MEP construction capacity. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation. The key diligence issue is separating durable bottleneck revenue from cyclical backlog, one-time hyperscaler pull-forward, acquisition effects, and margin normalization.
